notes.text: The app suite: one card per product family, each with its icon and name over a blue rule and its apps listed as links. An optional centered copy block (title, paragraph, text link) sits above the cards.
**Heading:** SemiBold 24px (`h3`), line height 1.3, −2%; Title Case, at most 60 characters.
notes.was: **Heading:** SemiBold 24px, line height 1.1, −2%; Title Case, at most 60 characters.

notes.text: **CTA:** the blue text link (blue label and arrow, `link-primary`), 24px under the content (16px on a card with no icon and no badge). Every card's CTA is blue, so links read the same in any row of cards.
notes.was: **CTA:** the neutral text link (charcoal label, blue arrow), 24px under the content (16px on a card with no icon and no badge).

notes.text: **In a row:** cards share the row's height, and the CTA (with the tags or badge above it) sits on the bottom edge, so the links line up across the row however long each card's copy is. This holds in any row (a CardModule, a `.q-grid` in a page, a carousel, or a card in its own wrapper), not only in CardModule.
**Provide:** the cards as children, a `label` that names the set ("Latest resources"), and optionally `variant="single"`, `slideWidth`, a `title` and a `link`.
notes.was: **Provide:** the cards as children, a `label` that names the set ("Latest resources"), and optionally `variant="single"` or `slideWidth`.

notes.text: **Heading:** `title` puts a heading over the cards in `h2` (SemiBold 38px, 740px wide at most) on the content column, 100px from the top of the section. `link` (`"View All Resources"` or `{ label, href }`) adds a neutral TextLink with an arrow at its right, on the heading's last line; on phones it wraps under the heading. The cards start 32px below. The heading also names the carousel for screen readers when there is no `label`.

notes.text: A banner for an event or a series of them: the series name in spaced capitals beside a thin rule, then a blue Tag ("Live Virtual Event") and the title, with one Button at the right. It sits over a light picture or a silent, looping video.
A checklist of what a product or plan includes: a blue check before each item, in columns, usually on a white card beside a copy block ("More Than Just a License to Scan").

**Columns:** `[{ id, name, logo, subtitle }]`. Give every column its `logo`; without one a dashed slot holds the name (as in the preview, where competitor logos are placeholders). **Min 1, max 5** competitors beside Qualys; columns past the fifth competitor are left out, because the marks get too narrow to scan. Two to five read best on desktop.

notes.text: `submitted` swaps the card's heading, fields, opt-in, button and consent line for an inline SuccessConfirmation: the green tick, the title, the message and one button. Any `banner` stays, so the card keeps its look before and after. Give the confirmation's text in `success` (`{ title, message, actionLabel, href }`; `type` is `download` unless you say `general`).
The confirmation sits on the card's own ground, with no second panel or shadow, and the card keeps its width. It is announced to screen readers as a status.
`submitted` is yours to set: show it from `onSubmit` once the request has gone through. For a popup instead, use SuccessConfirmation on its own.

notes.text: `pauseButton`: `true` (default) · What shows: The 44px pause button at the right of the heading · Use it when: Every page, unless the design calls for a clean heading row

`pauseButton`: `false` · What shows: No button. It comes into view only when it gets keyboard focus, so keyboard and screen reader users can still stop the row · Use it when: The heading row must stay clear, such as a centered heading
With the button hidden, the row still pauses under the pointer and when a logo link has focus, and it stays still for anyone who has reduced motion turned on.

**Hidden pause button (known problem):** WCAG 2.2.2 asks for a visible way to pause anything that moves on its own for more than five seconds. With `pauseButton={false}` the row pauses on hover and stays still with reduced motion, and keyboard users can reach the button, but a mouse user who only wants it to stop has to keep the pointer on it. Keep the button wherever you can.

On white, use the full-color Qualys logo, not the reversed one. The heading is `h2` (SemiBold 38px, line height 1.1, −2%), 8px above the subtitle in `paragraph-rg` Medium; both `text-inverted`. A column with a `logo` shows it in place of the heading: the reversed Qualys logo, 37px tall.

notes.text: With one or two items there is nothing to scroll to, so the module drops the carousel. The cards share one row and fill the content column (two at half width each, 24px apart; one at the full width), with no progress bar or buttons, and 100px above and below. Each card keeps its size (`lg`, `sm` or `video`) and its height matches the tallest. On phones the cards stack, 16px apart. Three or more quotes always use the carousel.
Use it once per page. A single quote can also be a TestimonialCard on its own in a section.

notes.text: **On cards, it's blue.** The call to action that ends a card (Card, ResourceCard, TestimonialCard, HoverCard) is always the blue text link with its arrow, never the neutral one, so links read the same across every row of cards.
Use: **AppGrid** · When: The app suite: a card per product family with its apps as links, under centered copy. For platform and overview pages.
Use: **FeatureList** · When: A checklist of what a product or plan includes, beside a copy block and one button.
Use: **StatCard** (plain) · When: One or two figures inside a copy block, beside a picture, with no card.

Use: **TestimonialCarousel** · When: Customer quotes or video stories. Use the video version when you have recordings. With fewer than three quotes it shows them as cards that fill the row instead of a carousel.
notes.was: When: Customer quotes or video stories. Use the video version when you have recordings.

notes.text: Use: **Carousel** · When: A row of resources, events or blog posts people browse sideways ("Latest Resources"). Give it a `title` and a "View All" `link` for the heading row above the cards.
notes.was: When: A row of resources, events or blog posts people browse sideways ("Latest Resources").

notes.text: After a form, show **SuccessConfirmation** in its place, rather than sending people to a new page. A Form's `submitted` state does this inside the card and keeps its banner.
notes.was: After a form, show **SuccessConfirmation** in its place, rather than sending people to a new page.

notes.text: Use: **SpeakerList** · When: Who is speaking, as small photos with names and roles, inside a Hero, an EventBanner or a copy block. Not a card: use ProfileCard when people need a bio or a link.

Keep one kind of card per row. Mixing a ResourceCard and a BlogCard in one carousel is fine; mixing a Card with a ResourceCard is not. Cards in a row share one height, with their calls to action lined up along the bottom, and a card's text-link CTA is always blue.
notes.was: Keep one kind of card per row. Mixing a ResourceCard and a BlogCard in one carousel is fine; mixing a Card with a ResourceCard is not.

notes.text: Use: **EventBanner** · When: Promoting an event or a series inside the page: series name, a tag, the title and one button, over a light picture or video.

**Rows of cards** (stat cards, Card Module, profile grids): pick the number across so rows come out full, and never leave one card alone on a row when another number avoids it: five are 3 + 2, not 4 + 1; four on tablet are 2 × 2, not 3 + 1. A row that still comes out short is centered, with its cards at the same width as the rows above. Listings that grow, such as search results or the events grid with Load More, keep their reading order and start each row on the left. Cards in a row share one height, and each card's call to action (text link, button or footer) sits on its bottom edge, so the calls to action line up across the row however long each card's copy is, wherever the row sits: a Card Module, a grid in a page or a carousel. A card's text link is always blue (see Buttons and links).

A row that still comes out short is centered, with its cards at the same width as the rows above.
